admission.justification: Concurrent commands can leave unrecorded processes or stop the winner runtime; a killed start can leave provision in progress, so canonical directory locking and descriptor inheritance prevent overlapping owners.

applicability: The PNT build, start, stop and reset command owner and its inherited provision-child descriptor.
conditions: The selected sandbox command is running on Linux with readable process or source observations; otherwise its named refusal applies.
exclusions: Build tool-server and native stop children do not inherit the lock after an abruptly killed parent.
An orphaned provision that hangs keeps commands refused until it ends.
statement: `build`, `start`, `stop` and `reset` hold one exclusive lock per sandbox, on the file `<sandbox>.lock` beside the directory, for the whole command; a second command does not wait but refuses with exit 2 and names the holder; the provision run of a start inherits the locked file and is named in the holder record, so a start that is killed while it provisions leaves the sandbox locked until that run has ended; `check` takes no lock.
